solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Effects of drinks: time off for bit of rest

indicators.note: the time letter goes off and the new letter stands in for it

parts.note: to tipple is to drink, so tipples are drinks

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired drinker reflects on what a few drinks do once the working day is over and it is time to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripples are the spreading consequences of an action, its knock-on effects.

clue.text: Long to tuck into wine? Got to!

indicators.note: the longing is tucked inside the wine

parts.note: red is red wine
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to tuck into some wine and decides they simply must.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reached a place is to have got to it.

clue.text: PM you send in error for Slormgorm?

definitions.note: the setter's crossword name, an example of an alias

indicators.note: sent by mistake, so the letters arrive jumbled

explanation.surface: A private message sent by mistake to the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Slormgorm is the setter of this puzzle, and a setter's byline is a pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is a false name used by an author, such as a setter's byline.

clue.text: Drop of liquor with port gets you loaded

indicators.note: a drop of the word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken as the drop
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits with some port leaves you drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the fortified wine but is the Yemeni harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded or burdened.

clue.text: Rock bands finally meeting with R. Wood?

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
and means with or together with
Ronnie Wood is a guitarist in the Rolling Stones, so one Stone

explanation.surface: Rock groups meet up with Ronnie Wood of the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and bands set up a music scene, but Rock is the definition: a type of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of compacted sand grains.

clue.text: Sack found in hansom by back of The Savoy?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by example

parts.note: a hansom is a horse-drawn cab
a sack is a kind of bag

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bag left in a horse-drawn cab outside the famous Savoy hotel in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is a London hotel, but here it is the crinkly-leaved Savoy variety of the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoy is a well-known variety of the green leafy vegetable with crinkled leaves.

clue.text: Nags and fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: complains or finds fault
second meaning: more than one of a freshwater fish

explanation.walkthrough: Nags suggests horses, but it is the verb for persistent complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to cavil, and carp are also freshwater fish.

clue.text: Cup-holder is more insolent close to game

parts.note: brassy means brazen or insolent, so brassier is more so

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rude sports fan near a match is holding a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cup-holder suggests a sports trophy winner; it is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, an undergarment whose cups hold the breasts.

clue.text: A composer's not unknown in this

definitions.text: A composer's not unknown in this

indicators.note: not means without, so the unknown is left out

parts.note: Liszt was a Hungarian composer, with the 's read as 'is'
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A famous composer is far from unknown: he belongs on this list.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the wordplay and the description of the celebrity list.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the roster of top celebrities, where the famous rather than obscure belong.

clue.text: Something very ugly I saw broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken over the air, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: said in a British accent, these two words sound like a word for an ugly sight

explanation.surface: A viewer describes a hideous thing they saw on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where the final R is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: A person in charge at the front

parts.note: a head is the person in charge, as of a school

explanation.surface: A description of a leader positioned at the front of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead is to be in front, leading the others.

clue.text: A theologian featuring in local story

indicators.note: the article and the cleric appear inside the other word

parts.note: a local is a native of the place
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop, taken loosely as a churchman or theologian

explanation.surface: A tale from the area that happens to include a religious scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

clue.text: Fun-seekers fellow placed in bank jobs

indicators.note: the college fellow is set inside the robberies

parts.note: a heist is a robbery, such as a bank job
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Thrill-seekers who take part in bank robberies, with a fellow brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonists pursue pleasure as their chief aim, so they are seekers of fun.

clue.text: Row of offset tools

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters running across these two words

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A neat line of tools that have been set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument, a row.

clue.text: Italian leader touring north's an idiot

indicators.note: the leader travels round the compass point, enclosing it

parts.note: Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's fascist leader
N for north, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A jibe that an Italian leader travelling around the north is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, a fool.

clue.text: It's a job and it comes with no rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A job advert boasting the post comes free of any nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist is a professional who studies the economy, so the word names an occupation.

clue.text: Those none represented precisely

indicators.note: re-presented, so the letters are shown again in another order

explanation.surface: A cryptic-sounding statement that those people were represented by no one at all.
explanation.definitionFit: On the nose is an idiom meaning exactly or precisely.

clue.text: Offensive kid gets hit for four-letter word

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 attack in the Vietnam War
to rag is to tease or kid
to ram is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A rude child gets a smack for swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Four-letter word suggests swearing, but it is a literal description.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is a word of four letters, from Greek tetra meaning four.

clue.text: Self-serving sanction I sorted out

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: A self-interested ruling I approved after fixing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Self-serving looks like selfish, but here it is a cheeky literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Onanistic relates to masturbation, gratifying oneself, and by extension means self-indulgent.

clue.text: Contest concerning NHS department or unit?

definitions.note: the question mark marks the hospital-unit misdirection

parts.note: comp is short for competition, a contest
on means about or concerning
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a contest about a hospital department counts as a unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks like a hospital unit to go with NHS department, but it means a part of a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A component is a single constituent part, a unit within a larger whole.

clue.text: Share digs about old nun's clothing

parts.note: a habit is a nun's robe

explanation.surface: Housemates make fun of an old nun's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British for lodgings; 'share digs' could read as jointly poking fun. C is circa, about.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together, sharing a home.

clue.text: Old Bill given the greenlight to be strict

parts.note: ex- means former or old
a parliamentary bill that is approved becomes an Act

explanation.surface: The police, the Old Bill, are given approval to crack down hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police, but here the words split: old, and a bill that is passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact can mean rigorous or precise, demanding strict accuracy.

clue.text: Game hard tenor and nurse make more strict

parts.note: tig is the children's chasing game also called tag
EN is an Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: A tough game involving a tenor and a nurse tightens the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten rules is to make them stricter.

clue.text: Ship possibly carrying dangerous beast

indicators.note: the two words carry the answer within their letters

parts.note: the answer runs from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A vessel perhaps transporting a hazardous animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is notoriously one of Africa's most dangerous large animals.

clue.text: Intrinsically, a short group

parts.note: per means a, as in so much a head

indicators.note: short means lacking its final letter

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Something is essentially a small group.
explanation.definitionFit: Per se is Latin for by itself, meaning intrinsically.

clue.text: Looking fierce enthrals Catholic husband

indicators.note: to enthral is here to hold inside, so the first word surrounds the others

parts.note: searing heat is fierce heat

explanation.surface: A fierce gaze captivates a Catholic husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching means seeking or looking for something.

clue.text: Barman posed with half-cut Okie

definitions.note: a man of bars, a composer of music in bars

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, leaving its back half

explanation.surface: A bartender posed for a picture with a drunk Oklahoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Okie is slang for someone from Oklahoma; half-cut is British slang for drunk. Barman is not a bartender here but a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, and composers write music measured in bars.

clue.text: Hard to give support to fool in clergy

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting letter sits below the other piece

parts.note: a clot is a fool

explanation.surface: It is hard to back a fool among the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is a collective term for the clergy, from their clerical dress.

clue.text: Lawyer right to go after dodgy arbiters

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed after the rearranged letters
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A lawyer is set right after some crooked referees.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who argues cases in the higher courts in Britain.

clue.text: Group books film about Casablanca's lead

indicators.note: these two pieces go round the next letter

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A set of books on films covers the star of Casablanca.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially eight musicians.

clue.text: Room where doctor opens case in house

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the operating ..., where a surgeon opens up a patient

explanation.surface: A doctor opens a case file in a room at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is a patient here, and 'opens' means surgery, not opening a file.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is a surgical room, and a theatre is also a building where plays are staged.

clue.text: Complain about drunken outburst in High Barnet

indicators.note: the complaint wraps round the drunk's noise

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is the sound of a drunken hiccup

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a drunk making noise in High Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a London place name; split here, barnet is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), so a high barnet is a tall hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a hairstyle with a tall central crest of hair, so a high hairdo.
